concept_map.chapter_overview: Aaj hum NCERT Class 9 Mathematics ke Chapter 9 — वृत्त (Circles) — ko padhenge. Ismein jeeva (chord) dwara kendra aur circumference par antarit kon, kendra se jeeva par lamb, barabar jeevaon ki kendra se dooriyan, aur chaap dwara antarit kon (Theorem 9.1 se 9.8) aate hain. Proofs triangle congruence (SSS, SAS, SSS/RHS ideas) aur CPCT (सर्वांगसम त्रिभुजों के संगत भाग) par based hain — exam mein bahut scoring chapter!
concept_map.welcome: Good morning, bacchon! Smart Board par aaj ek circular adventure — वृत्त! School ke ground ka round park, cycle ka tyre, thali ka man — sab circles hain. Aaj hum prove karenge ki barabar jeevaen kendra par barabar kon banati hain, lamb jeeva ko bisect karta hai, aur chaap ka kendriya kon periphery wale kon ka duguna hota hai. Notebook, compass aur scale ready? Chalo shuru karte hain!
learning_outcomes: Jeeva dwara kisi bindu / kendra par antarit kon ko pehchanna aur Theorem 9.1–9.2 (barabar jeeva ↔ barabar kendriya kon) apply karna
Kendra se jeeva par lamb aur uske vilom (Theorem 9.3–9.4) se jeeva ke segments aur perpendicularity prove karna
Barabar jeevaon ki kendra se dooriyan (Theorem 9.5–9.6) aur pratichhedi jeevaon wale applications solve karna
Chaap dwara antarit kon, Theorem 9.7 (kendra par kon = 2 × periphery par kon), Theorem 9.8 (same segment) aur ardhvritt ka samakon yaad rakhna

generated.concept: जीवा द्वारा एक बिन्दु पर अंतरित कोण
generated.say: Bacchon, pehle basic language clear karte hain — warna theorems mein confuse ho jaoge. NCERT kehti hai: ek rekha-khand AB lo, aur ek bindu P jo AB par na ho. AP aur BP milao. Jo kon APB banta hai, use hum kehte hain — rekha-khand AB dwara bindu P par antarit kon (angle subtended by the line segment AB at point P). Simple! Ab circle mein socho. Chord AB lo. Agar P circle ke centre O par ho, toh ∠AOB wahi kon hai jo chord AB kendra par antarit karti hai — angle subtended by the chord at the centre. Agar P major arc AB par ho, toh ∠APB major arc wale side se antarit kon hai; agar minor arc par koi point C ho, toh ∠ACB minor arc side se antarit kon. Aakriti 9.2 mein yeh teen alag situations dikhti hain. Ab interesting observation: agar tum circle mein alag-alag jeevaen khinchoge aur unke kendriya kon measure karoge, toh dikhega — jeeva jitni badi, kendra par antarit kon utna bada. Diameter sabse badi jeeva hai, toh uska kendriya kon 180 degree tak ja sakta hai (semi-circle case). Chhoti jeeva → chhota central angle. Yeh intuition aage Theorem 9.1 ke liye foundation hai. Classroom tip: hamesha figure mein clearly likho — 'kon kis jeeva dwara kis bindu par antarit ho raha hai'. Exam mein language galat hone se marks kate jaate hain. Yaad rakho teen jagah: (1) kisi general point par, (2) centre par, (3) circumference / arc par. Aaj se 'antarit kon' bolte hi dimaag mein triangle APB ya AOB flash hona chahiye!
generated.example: Classroom ke round wall-clock par do numbers (jaise 12 aur 4) ko chord se jodo — centre se bana kon central angle hai; rim par kisi teesre number se bana kon periphery par antarit kon hai.

generated.concept: प्रमेय 9.1 व 9.2 – बराबर जीवाएँ और केन्द्र पर कोण
generated.say: Ab activity! Circle mein do ya adhik barabar jeevaen khincho, centre O se unke endpoints jodo, aur kendriya kon measure karo. NCERT kehti hai — tum paoge ki barabar jeevaen kendra par barabar kon antarit karti hain. Isi ko theorem banate hain. Pramey 9.1: Vritt ki barabar jeevaen kendra par barabar kon antarit karti hain. Proof (aakriti 9.4): Diya hai circle centre O, equal chords AB aur CD, yani AB = CD. Siddh karna hai ∠AOB = ∠COD. Triangles AOB aur COD mein: OA = OC (dono radii), OB = OD (dono radii), aur AB = CD (diya hai). Toh SSS rule se △AOB ≅ △COD. CPCT se ∠AOB = ∠COD. Bahut clean proof! Tip: NCERT bolti hai 'सर्वांगसम त्रिभुजों के संगत भाग' ko short mein CPCT likhenge — aage bahut use hoga. Ab converse socho — agar do jeevaen kendra par barabar kon antarit karen, kya jeevaen barabar hongi? Tracing paper activity: circle cut karke chakki banao, centre par do equal angles AOB aur POQ banao, chords ke along segments kaato, overlap karo — woh fully cover karte hain, matlab chords equal. Pramey 9.2: Yadi ek vritt ki jeevaon dwara kendra par antarit kon barabar hon, to ve jeevaen barabar hoti hain. Yeh Theorem 9.1 ka vilom hai. Proof idea: aakriti 9.4 mein agar ∠AOB = ∠COD lo, toh radii equal hone se SAS/ASA type se triangles congruent, phir CPCT se AB = CD. Exercise 9.1 mein congruent circles (equal radii) ke liye bhi same results extend hote hain — barabar jeevaen centres par barabar kon, aur vilom. Yaad: equal chords ↔ equal central angles — if and only if!

Pramey 9.2 (vilom): ∠AOB = ∠COD ⇒ AB = CD

generated.say: Section 9.2 — bahut favourite exam topic! Activity: tracing paper par circle centre O, chord AB khincho. Paper ko O se guzarne wali line ke along aise fold karo ki chord ka ek hissa doosre par pade. Fold mark AB ko M par kaate. NCERT kehti hai ∠OMA = ∠OMB = 90°, yani OM, AB par lamb (perpendicular) hai. Aur haan — M, A aur B ke beech midpoint hota hai, isliye AM = MB. Isi observation ko theorem banate hain. Pramey 9.3: Ek vritt ke kendra se ek jeeva par dala gaya lamb jeeva ko samadvibhajit karta hai. Proof khud do (NCERT bolti hai): OA aur OB milao; right triangles OMA aur OMB congruent (radii + right angle + common OM) se AM = MB. Ab vilom socho carefully. Theorem 9.3 mein diya = kendra se lamb; siddh = jeeva bisect. Isliye vilom mein: diya = kendra se guzarne wali rekha jeeva ko bisect kare; siddh = woh rekha jeeva par lamb hai. Pramey 9.4: Ek vritt ke kendra se ek jeeva ko samadvibhajit karne ke liye khinchi gayi rekha jeeva par lamb hoti hai. Proof sketch (aakriti 9.7): AB chord, M midpoint, OM join. △OMA aur △OMB mein: OA = OB (radii — kyon?), AM = MB (M midpoint — kyon?), OM = OM (common). SSS se triangles congruent. CPCT se ∠OMA = ∠OMB. Magar yeh adjacent angles ek seedhi rekha AB par hain, isliye har ek 90° — OM ⊥ AB. Classroom tip: 'bisect' aur 'perpendicular' alag cheezein hain; yahan dono linked hain jab line centre se jaati hai. Diameter special case: centre khud diameter par hai, toh distance zero — baad ke section mein kaam aayega.

generated.say: Pehle 'doorí' clear karo. Line AB aur bahar point P — P se AB ke har point tak segments ban sakte hain, lekin sabse chhota kaunsa? Woh perpendicular segment PM hota hai. Mathematics mein: ek bindu se ek rekha ki doori = us bindu se rekha par dale gaye lamb ki lambai. Agar bindu rekha par ho, doori shunya. Ab circle mein: lambe jeevaen centre ke kareeb hoti hain; chhoti jeevaen door. Diameter sabse badi jeeva — centre us par hi hai, doori zero! Activity (aakriti 9.9): do equal chords AB, CD; O se perpendiculars OM, ON. Fold/overlap se milta hai OM = ON. Congruent circles par bhi same. Pramey 9.5: Ek vritt ki (ya sarvaangasam vritton ki) barabar jeevaen kendra se (ya kendron se) saman doori par hoti hain. Vilom activity (aakriti 9.10): centre se do equal lengths OX, OY khincho, un par perpendicular chords PQ, RS banao — measure karo, PQ = RS. Pramey 9.6: Ek vritt ke kendra se samadursth jeevaen lambai mein saman hoti hain. Matlab: equal chords ⇔ equidistant from centre. Link Theorem 9.3 se: perpendicular distance hi 'doorí' hai, aur woh chord ko bisect bhi karti hai — isliye half-chord aur distance Pythagoras se jude hote hain. Agar do chords equal, unke half equal, radii equal, toh distances equal. Classroom tip: 'doorí' hamesha perpendicular length; schiefe (slant) distance mat lo. Exam mein concentric circles wale questions bhi isi family se aate hain.

generated.say: Ab Theorems 9.5–9.6 ka application — NCERT Example 1. Statement: Yadi ek vritt ki do pratichhedi jeevaen, pratichhed bindu se guzarne wale vyas se saman kon banayen, to siddh karo ki ve jeevaen barabar hain. Figure 9.11: centre O, chords AB aur CD point M par intersect; diameter PQ M se guzarta hai; diya ∠AMP = ∠DMP. Siddh: AB = CD. Strategy: AB aur CD par O se perpendiculars OX aur OY dalo. Phir triangles OXM aur OYM mein angles chase karke dikhao OX = OY, phir Theorem 9.6 se chords equal. Detail: triangle angle sum se ∠XOM = 180° − 90° − ∠XMO = 90° − ∠XMO. Diya ∠AMP = ∠DMP se related angles equal nikalte hain, aur eventually ∠XOM = ∠YOM. Triangles OXM, OYM mein: ∠XMO = ∠YMO (given path), ∠XOM = ∠YOM (proved), OM common — ASA/AAS se congruent, CPCT se OX = OY. Equal distances from centre ⇒ AB = CD (Theorem 9.6). Yeh pattern yaad rakho: prove distances equal → conclude chords equal. Exercise 9.2 mein related apps: common chord of intersecting circles (radii 5 cm, 3 cm, centres 4 cm apart), equal chords intersecting inside → segments equal; line through concentric circles → intercepted equal chords; park pe girls Reshma-Salma-Mandeep equilateral idea; circular park Ankur-Saiyed-David equally spaced → chord length of equilateral inscribed triangle. Numerical tip for Q1: common chord ⊥ line of centres aur bisected; use two Pythagoras equations.
generated.example: Do crossing ropes across a round fountain — agar diameter rope se same angles banayen, crossing ropes equal length honge (Example 1 idea).

Bridge: prove OX = OY (distances) → Th. 9.6 → AB = CD
Tool kit: ⊥ from centre, congruence, Th. 9.5/9.6

worked_example.problem: Do vritt, trijya 5 cm aur 3 cm, do binduon par pratichhed; kendron ke beech doori 4 cm. Ubhayanishth jeeva (common chord) ki lambai gyat karo. (Ex 9.2 Q1)
steps: Centres O, O′; common chord AB; OO′ = 4 cm, OA = 5 cm, O′A = 3 cm. OO′ chord AB ko M par bisect karta hai aur ⊥ hai.
OM = x, O′M = 4 − x. Pythagoras: 5² − x² = 3² − (4 − x)² ⇒ 25 − x² = 9 − (16 − 8x + x²) ⇒ 25 = 8x − 7 ⇒ x = 4.
OM = 4 cm ⇒ M, O′ par; AM = √(O′A² − O′M²) = √(9 − 0) = 3 cm (ya √(5² − 4²) = 3). Isliye AB = 2 × AM = 6 cm.

easy: Example 1 ka kathan apne shabdon mein likho.
medium: Example 1 mein OX = OY prove karne ke baad AB = CD kis theorem se aata hai?
hard: Yadi ek rekha do sankendri vritton (centre O) ko A, B, C, D par kaate (order A,B,C,D), siddh karo AB = CD. (Ex 9.2 Q4)

generated.say: Section 9.4 shuru! Chord ke endpoints (diameter chhodkar) circle ko do chaapon mein baantte hain — ek dirgh (major) aur ek laghu (minor). Sawal: barabar jeevaen lo, unke corresponding arcs ke baare mein kya kahoge? Sirf length equal? NCERT kehti hai — aur bhi zyada: agar ek arc ko doosre par rakho bina ainthhe-mode, toh woh fully cover karte hain — matlab arcs congruent (sarvaangasam) hain. Activity: chord CD ke corresponding arc ko CD along cut karke equal chord AB ke arc par rakho — cover ho jaata hai. Result: barabar jeevaen sarvaangasam chaap banati hain; vilomatah sarvaangasam chaap barabar jeevaen banate hain. Formal: Yadi kisi vritt ki do jeevaen barabar hon, to unke sangata chaap sarvaangasam hote hain; vilomatah yadi do chaap sarvaangasam hon, to unki sangata jeevaen barabar hoti hain. Ab 'chaap dwara kendra par antarit kon': minor arc central angle antarit karta hai; major arc corresponding reflex central angle antarit karta hai. Aakriti 9.14 mein minor arc PQ → ∠POQ; major arc PQ → reflex ∠POQ. Theorem 9.1 ke saath jodo: congruent/equal arcs bhi kendra par barabar kon antarit karte hain. Aur: jeeva dwara kendra par antarit kon = uske corresponding (minor) arc dwara kendra par antarit kon. Yeh bridge agle Theorem 9.7 ke liye zaroori hai — wahan hum arc ke central angle ko circumference ke angle se compare karenge. Classroom tip: hamesha specify karo minor ya major arc; warna reflex angle bhool jaate ho.

generated.say: Ab chapter ka star theorem! Pramey 9.7: Ek chaap dwara kendra par antarit kon, vritt ke shesh bhag ke kisi bindu par antarit kon ka duguna hota hai. Matlab: central angle = 2 × inscribed angle (same arc). Diya: arc PQ, centre O → ∠POQ; remaining circumference par point A → ∠PAQ. Siddh: ∠POQ = 2∠PAQ. Teen cases (aakriti 9.15): (i) PQ minor arc, (ii) PQ semicircle, (iii) PQ major arc. Proof idea — teeno mein OA ko milaakar B tak badhao (O se A through, diameter direction). Exterior angle theorem: ∠BOQ = ∠OAQ + ∠AQO. △OAQ mein OA = OQ (radii) ⇒ base angles equal ⇒ ∠OAQ = ∠AQO. Isliye ∠BOQ = 2∠OAQ ... (1). Similarly ∠BOP = 2∠OAP ... (2). (1)+(2): ∠POQ = 2∠PAQ. Case (iii) major arc mein result reflex ∠POQ = 2∠PAQ hota hai. Note: agar chord PQ banao, toh ∠PAQ ko vritt-khand (segment) PAQP mein bana kon bhi kehte hain. Yeh theorem exams mein numerical + proof dono mein aata hai — 'find angle at centre if angle at circumference is ...' ya reverse. Classroom memory: same arc dekho; centre wala hamesha double. Agar alag arcs, formula apply mat karo! Numerical tip: agar circumference par 40° diya ho toh centre 80°; agar centre 150° (minor) ho toh circumference 75°. Semicircle case mein centre 180° ⇒ circumference 90° — next concept mein detail.

generated.say: Theorem 9.7 se turant ek beautiful corollary nikalta hai. Agar remaining part par do points A aur B lo (aakriti 9.16), toh ∠POQ = 2∠PAQ = 2∠PBQ. Isliye ∠PAQ = ∠PBQ. Matlab same arc ke inscribed angles equal. Isi ko kehte hain — Pramey 9.8: Ek hi vritt-khand (segment) ke kon barabar hote hain. Angles in the same segment of a circle are equal. Ab special case — semicircle. Agar arc PQ semicircle hai, toh central ∠POQ = 180°. Theorem 9.7 se inscribed ∠PAQ = (1/2)×180° = 90°. Koi bhi point A semicircle par lo, ∠PAQ = 90°. Famous result: Ardhvritt ka kon samakon hota hai — The angle in a semicircle is a right angle. Yeh Class 9–10 exams ka evergreen fact hai! Theorem 9.8 ka vilom bhi satya hai (NCERT mention): agar do angles equal hain appropriate configuration mein, toh points same segment mein lie karte hain — details aage/related results mein. Revision package of chapter: (1) equal chords ↔ equal central angles, (2) ⊥ from centre bisects chord (and converse), (3) equal chords ↔ equidistant from centre, (4) central = 2 × inscribed, (5) same segment angles equal, (6) angle in semicircle = 90°. Board par yeh cheh lines likh lo — poora chapter revise! Practice: semicircle diameter endpoints A,B; rim point C → ∠ACB = 90° hamesha. Numericals mein diameter pehchano pehle.
